name: isColor
summary: Returns the value when every part of it is a colour, and raises when one is not.

arguments.name: $value
accepts: a colour, in any colour space, or transparent
a list of colours, which comes back with the separator it was given
var() and currentColor are refused: tint and shade pass the result to color.mix, which needs a real colour

caveats: `isNumber` and `isTime` were brought into line for 4.0.0 and this was left behind. It kept their three faults: `isColor(())` reached Sass's own `Invalid index 1 for a list with 0 elements`, because `@for $i from 1 through 0` counts down rather than running no times; the message interpolated the item rather than inspecting it, so `isColor(null)` said `'' is not a color value`; and it was the only error in the library written in that shape, single-quoted and naming neither the function nor the argument.
It returns the value it was given since 4.0.0. It used to rebuild it as a comma list, so `isColor(red blue)` answered `red, blue`. A single colour emits the same CSS either way.

`var()` and `currentColor` are refused on purpose. `tint` and `shade` pass the colour straight to `color.mix`, which needs a real colour, so widening this would move their failure to a Sass internal message. `scss/internal/_color-problem.scss` is the looser check the mixins use.
